Even if the available habitat for species does not change, one might consider potential changes to the performance of organisms. The spawning temperatures are provided for 14 of the 46 fish species listed in the Yadkin DLA. Two of these species, threadfin shad and golden shiner, spawn through August, the period for which this report has modeled reservoir changes due to coverage by FPV. The threadfin shad has a spawning temperature of 21°C while the Golden shiner spawns in 20–26.67°C. As summer temperatures (on average) already exceed the preferred spawning temperature for these species, a decline of 1.84–6.04°C in maximum temperature (Table 13) as a result of shading by FPV panels may be considered beneficial to reproduction for these species. Similar investigations of the match or mis-match between environmental conditions realized after coverage by FPV and the environmental tolerances or preferences of species of interest or concern could be conducted to determine expected direction and magnitude of change. This type of consideration could be applied to various species of interest when a triggering or threshold environmental condition is known.
